name: Sheet-metal pressing
summary: A press forms a flat steel sheet into a body panel in one stroke. The panels are then welded into a body.
how: Cut the steel sheet to size and load it into the die.
Close the press so that the sheet takes the shape of the die.
Weld the panels into one shell and grind the seams smooth.

origin.note: Budd makes the first all-steel car body in a press for Dodge.

adoptions.via: Large presses form the wings and the roof of a streamlined body in single panels.
Presses form deep panels, and the fin is a pressed shape welded to the rear wing.
Presses make the long bonnet and the short deck of the Mustang in large numbers.
Deep draws give the round, joined body of the small one-box car.
